strategy.summary: CART-12 prices the cart at checkout in src/cart.js: cartTotal applies a 10% bulk discount (10+ items by summed quantity), then the SAVE5 coupon ($5 off, goods floored at $0, other codes throw), then shipping ($4.99 unless discounted goods ≥ $50; empty cart free). Tests are vitest unit tests on cartTotal/bulkDiscount, focused on the boundaries. Reading the code, bulkDiscount uses `> BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items gets no discount, contrary to AC1 and to the constant's own doc comment ("at least this many"); that case is planned as an expected failure with a recorded defect.
inScope: cartTotal and bulkDiscount in src/cart.js: bulk discount threshold and rate, coupon order and floor, unknown coupon refusal, shipping threshold on discounted goods, empty cart
outOfScope: UI/checkout pages (none exist in the repo)
Coupon case-sensitivity and whitespace handling (not specified by the ticket)
assumptions: Prices are in dollars as plain numbers rounded to cents by the module; tests assert exact cent values with toBe.
Bulk discount and the $50 threshold are compared against the module's exported constants' documented meaning; tests use literal amounts from the ticket so a constant change is caught.
An unknown coupon is refused by cartTotal throwing an Error; the test checks the error message contains the submitted code, the part the test controls.
openQuestions: Should coupon codes be case-insensitive (e.g. 'save5')? The code treats them as case-sensitive; not tested.
Does SAVE5 count when the cart is empty? The code accepts it and charges $0; tested only that the empty cart costs nothing.

risks.description: Off-by-one at the 10-item threshold (code uses > instead of >=)
risks.mitigation: TC1 tests exactly 10 items spread across lines; TC2/TC3 bracket it with 9 and 11.

risks.description: Coupon applied before the bulk discount, or shipping judged on the undiscounted subtotal
risks.mitigation: TC4 picks amounts where order changes the total; TC9 picks a cart whose subtotal is ≥ $50 but discounted goods are below.

risks.description: Negative goods price when the coupon exceeds the subtotal
risks.mitigation: TC5 asserts the total is exactly shipping alone.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (summing each line's quantity) gets 10% off its subtotal; fewer than 10 gets no bulk discount.
Coupon SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount, the goods never cost less than $0, and any other coupon code is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when goods cost $50 or more after discounts, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs $0.

testCases.title: gives 10% off a cart of exactly 10 items spread across lines
testCases.expected: Total 90 (100 less 10%, free shipping). Currently the code returns 100 (uses > 10), so the test is marked expected-to-fail and a defect recorded.
testCases.rationale: Boundary of the bulk rule; also proves quantities are summed across lines.

testCases.title: gives no bulk discount to a cart of 9 items
testCases.expected: Total 90 (no discount, free shipping at exactly 90 ≥ 50).

testCases.title: gives 10% off a cart of 11 items
testCases.rationale: Happy path above the threshold, independent of the boundary defect.

testCases.title: takes SAVE5 off after the bulk discount
never prices the goods below $0 with SAVE5
refuses an unknown coupon code with an error
testCases.expected: Throws an Error whose message contains 'SAVE10'.
testCases.rationale: Refusal case for the coupon input.

testCases.title: ships free when the discounted goods cost exactly $50
charges $4.99 shipping when the goods cost $49.99
charges shipping when only the undiscounted subtotal reaches $50
charges nothing for an empty cart
testCases.rationale: Empty cart must not be charged shipping.

strategy.environmentNotes: Pure unit tests; no services. Run with `npm test` (vitest run).

defects.title: Cart of exactly 10 items gets no bulk discount
defects.description: AC1: a cart with 10 or more items in total should get 10% off. src/cart.js bulkDiscount uses `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD` (BULK_THRESHOLD = 10, documented as "at least this many"), so a cart of exactly 10 items is charged full price. Expected cartTotal([{price:10,quantity:4},{price:10,quantity:6}]) = 90; actual 100.
defects.evidence: TC1 is marked it.fails; the assertion expect(cartTotal(items)).toBe(90) fails because the result is 100 (attempt 0, 10 passed including the expected failure). Fix: change `>` to `>=` at src/cart.js:22.
